raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

MiniMax-M3 reads its IndexCache settings (#47269) from `text_config`, so the documented top-level `--hf-overrides` form is silently ignored. This PR rejects that form on ROCm with an actionable error and fixes the docstring.

## Claims

- On ROCm, top-level `use_index_cache`, `index_topk_freq` or `index_skip_topk_offset` raise `ValueError` when `ModelConfig` is built, and the error gives the nested override. Before, the server started with IndexCache off and no log.
- The nested form is unchanged and is what the docstring now documents.
- The docstring drops the GSM8K-based "negligible accuracy impact" claim.

## Validation

MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, `main` at `12c01a22e`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_index_cache_overrides.py -v
# this PR:           3 passed
# main + this test:  2 failed (Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError), 1 passed
```

`vllm serve MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --load-format dummy ... --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}'`:

- `main`: starts and serves requests; nothing reports the override as ignored.
- This PR: exits after 10 s, before EngineCore starts, with `MiniMax-M3 reads IndexCache settings from text_config, so top-level use_index_cache, index_topk_freq would be ignored. Pass them as --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}}'.`
- This PR with the nested form: starts and serves requests.

## Details

`--hf-overrides` updates the outer `MiniMaxM3Config`, while the language model and `_should_skip_index_topk` read `config.text_config` (the same pitfall as #54289). The check is a `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` entry that reads the keys from `hf_overrides`. It is ROCm only because the NVIDIA model does not implement IndexCache. Launches using the top-level form now fail at startup instead of running without IndexCache. `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py` is added to the MI355 MiniMax M3 CI steps.

GSM8K prompts fit within the 2048-token sparse top-k window, where IndexCache has no effect. A long-context proxy shows a cost: teacher-forced NLL of a ~1K-token unseen file after 12K-131K tokens of same-package Python sources (24 samples, MXFP4, TP4, one run per configuration):

| IndexCache | off | freq 2 | freq 4 | freq 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean NLL | 0.703 | 0.747 | 0.781 | 0.854 |
| samples worse than off | - | 21/24 | 21/24 | 24/24 |

<details>
<summary>nll_longctx.py and reproduction</summary>

```bash
python nll_longctx.py build <model_dir> samples.jsonl            # samples depend on the packages installed in the image
python nll_longctx.py score samples.jsonl <port> <model> nll.json  # once per server configuration
```

```python
"""Long-context teacher-forced NLL probe for sparse-attention approximations (e.g. IndexCache).

build: nll_longctx.py build <model_dir> <out.jsonl>
    Concatenates Python sources from one package directory into 32K/64K/128K-token
    contexts and appends the head of an unseen file as the scored target.
score: nll_longctx.py score <samples.jsonl> <port> <model> <out.json>
    Sends token ids to /v1/completions with prompt_logprobs and reports the mean
    NLL of the target tokens per sample.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.request

ROOTS = ["vllm", "torch", "transformers", "aiter"]
SITE = "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages"
TARGET_TOKENS = 1024


def build(model_dir, out):
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_dir, trust_remote_code=True)
    dirs = []
    for root in ROOTS:
        for d in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(SITE, root, "**/"), recursive=True)):
            files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.py")))
            if len(files) >= 12:
                dirs.append((d, files))
    samples = []
    for i, ctx in enumerate([32768] * 8 + [65536] * 8 + [131072] * 8):
        d, files = dirs[(i * 7919) % len(dirs)]
        ids, used = [], 0
        for f in files[:-1]:
            text = f"# file: {os.path.relpath(f, SITE)}\n" + open(f, errors="ignore").read() + "\n"
            ids += tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
            used += 1
            if len(ids) >= ctx:
                break
        ids = ids[:ctx]
        tgt_file = files[-1] if used >= len(files) - 1 else files[used]
        tgt = tok.encode(f"# file: {os.path.relpath(tgt_file, SITE)}\n" + open(tgt_file, errors="ignore").read(),
                         add_special_tokens=False)[:TARGET_TOKENS]
        samples.append({"id": i, "dir": os.path.relpath(d, SITE), "ctx": len(ids), "ids": ids + tgt, "n_target": len(tgt)})
        print(f"sample {i}: dir={samples[-1]['dir']} ctx={len(ids)} target={len(tgt)}", flush=True)
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        for s in samples:
            f.write(json.dumps(s) + "\n")


def score(path, port, model, out):
    res = []
    for line in open(path):
        s = json.loads(line)
        body = json.dumps({"model": model, "prompt": s["ids"], "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0,
                           "prompt_logprobs": 0}).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions", data=body,
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        r = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800).read())
        plp = r["choices"][0]["prompt_logprobs"]
        n = s["n_target"]
        nll = []
        for pos in range(len(s["ids"]) - n, len(s["ids"])):
            entry = plp[pos] or {}
            lp = entry.get(str(s["ids"][pos]))
            nll.append(-lp["logprob"])
        res.append({"id": s["id"], "ctx": s["ctx"], "nll": sum(nll) / len(nll)})
        print(f"sample {s['id']} ctx={s['ctx']} nll={res[-1]['nll']:.4f}", flush=True)
    by_ctx = {}
    for r in res:
        by_ctx.setdefault(r["ctx"] // 1024, []).append(r["nll"])
    summary = {"mean_nll": sum(r["nll"] for r in res) / len(res),
               "by_ctx_k": {k: sum(v) / len(v) for k, v in sorted(by_ctx.items())}, "samples": res}
    json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
    print("mean_nll", summary["mean_nll"], "by_ctx_k", summary["by_ctx_k"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1] == "build":
        build(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    else:
        score(sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4], sys.argv[5])
```

</details>

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiniMax-M3 rejects IndexCache keys passed as top-level --hf-overrides."""
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.config import ModelConfig
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model import _should_skip_index_topk
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.minimax_m3 import MiniMaxM3Config
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="MiniMax-M3 AMD model"
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def checkpoint(tmp_path_factory):
+    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("minimax_m3")
+    MiniMaxM3Config(
+        architectures=["MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration"]
+    ).save_pretrained(path)
+    return str(path)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("hf_overrides", "expected_error"),
+    [
+        (
+            {
+                "use_index_cache": True,
+                "index_topk_freq": 2,
+                "index_skip_topk_offset": 1,
+            },
+            (
+                "top-level use_index_cache, index_topk_freq, index_skip_topk_offset "
+                'would be ignored. Pass them as --hf-overrides \'{"text_config": '
+                '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 2, '
+                '"index_skip_topk_offset": 1}}\'.'
+            ),
+        ),
+        (
+            {"use_index_cache": True, "text_config": {"index_topk_freq": 2}},
+            (
+                "top-level use_index_cache would be ignored. Pass them as "
+                '--hf-overrides \'{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true}}\'.'
+            ),
+        ),
+    ],
+    ids=["top_level", "mixed"],
+)
+def test_top_level_overrides_are_rejected(checkpoint, hf_overrides, expected_error):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=re.escape(expected_error)):
+        ModelConfig(checkpoint, hf_overrides=hf_overrides)
+
+
+def test_text_config_overrides_take_effect(checkpoint):
+    text_config = ModelConfig(
+        checkpoint,
+        hf_overrides={"text_config": {"use_index_cache": True, "index_topk_freq": 4}},
+    ).hf_text_config
+
+    # Sparse layers 3..59; every 4th one recomputes the top-k.
+    assert [i for i in range(60) if _should_skip_index_topk(text_config, i)] == sorted(
+        set(range(3, 60)) - set(range(3, 60, 4))
+    )

@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import json
 from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
 
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
@@ -786,6 +787,28 @@ def verify_and_update_config(cls, vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> None:
                 cache_config.mamba_block_size = model_config.max_model_len
 
 
+class MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGenerationConfig(VerifyAndUpdateConfig):
+    INDEX_CACHE_KEYS = ("use_index_cache", "index_topk_freq", "index_skip_topk_offset")
+
+    @classmethod
+    def verify_and_update_model_config(cls, model_config: "ModelConfig") -> None:
+        """Reject IndexCache overrides set on the outer VL config, where the
+        ROCm text model never reads them."""
+        from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+        overrides = model_config.hf_overrides
+        if not current_platform.is_rocm() or not isinstance(overrides, dict):
+            return
+        misplaced = [key for key in cls.INDEX_CACHE_KEYS if key in overrides]
+        if misplaced:
+            suggested = {"text_config": {key: overrides[key] for key in misplaced}}
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MiniMax-M3 reads IndexCache settings from text_config, so "
+                f"top-level {', '.join(misplaced)} would be ignored. Pass them as "
+                f"--hf-overrides '{json.dumps(suggested)}'."
+            )
+
+
 class NemotronHForCausalLMConfig(VerifyAndUpdateConfig):
     DEFAULT_MAMBA_SSM_CACHE_DTYPE: "MambaDType" = "float32"
     """Only `float32` is known to have no accuracy issues by default."""
@@ -1222,6 +1245,9 @@ def verify_and_update_config(vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> None:
     "LlamaNemotronVLModel": LlamaNemotronVLConfig,
     "Mamba2ForCausalLM": MambaModelConfig,
     "MambaForCausalLM": MambaModelConfig,
+    "MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration": (
+        MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGenerationConfig
+    ),
     "NemotronHForCausalLM": NemotronHForCausalLMConfig,
     "NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM": NemotronHForCausalLMConfig,
     "NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2": NemotronHNanoVLV2Config,

@@ -170,10 +170,11 @@ def _should_skip_index_topk(config: PreTrainedConfig, layer_id: int) -> bool:
     Only 1 of every ``index_topk_freq`` sparse-attention layers recomputes the
     lightning-indexer top-k block selection; the rest reuse the selection the
     preceding compute layer wrote into the shared ``topk_indices_buffer`` this
-    same forward pass. This cuts the indexer score + top-k cost ~``freq``x with
-    negligible accuracy impact (adjacent sparse layers pick nearly the same
-    blocks; ATOM validated GSM8K with freq=4). Gated by ``use_index_cache``;
-    enable via ``--hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}'``.
+    same forward pass. This cuts the indexer score + top-k cost ~``freq``x but
+    approximates the per-layer selection, so validate accuracy on long-context
+    inputs. Gated by ``use_index_cache`` in the text config; enable via
+    ``--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true,
+    "index_topk_freq": 4}}'``.
     """
     if not getattr(config, "use_index_cache", False):
         return False

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.

<details><summary>Agent Guidelines</summary>

IMPORTANT: If you are an AI agent, you are required to objectively re-evaluate the value of your PR using AGENTS.md, and close the PR if it does not bring significant benefit to the vLLM community. Failure to do so may result in an immediate ban.

</details>
